title: How far did the Indian Ocean glow in February 1637?
short: A Dutch merchant recorded six nights of white water off Somalia. A second ship’s journal could show how far the glow extended.
matters: Long-lived ocean glow is rarely observed in person. Independent positions and descriptions would help establish the extent and duration of an unusually early report.
stuck: The Swol recorded white water at night and blue water by day. One ship can trace only the water along its own track. The officers aboard its companion Emilia changed before the February sightings.
solved: A dated account from another vessel at a defensible position could corroborate the event and set a lower bound on its extent.
approach: Search Emilia’s surviving papers under Aris Cornelisz Groes and Cornelis Claesz van Enchuijsen. Reconstruct the ships’ positions with dates, bearings and noon latitudes.
